newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - SGS-Thomson stock dips.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - SGS-Thomson stock dips.

text.p: SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV took a tumble in after hours trading on Thursday, falling to 73 off a close of 80-7/8 on news that it expects second quarter revenues to come in below analysts' expectations.
The Franco-Italian semiconductor maker also predicted that its second quarter earnings would be in range with the previous quarter, but that second half market conditions should improve.
The company's share fell by some five percent in April after it reported a first quarter earnings decline due to price erosion.
Otherwise, after hours trading was quiet; "That's the only big mover right now," a dealer said.

Halts remained on Home State and Storage Dimensions stock. Home State, an auto insurance company, said late on Thursday that its units will cease writing new insurance business and that it is unlikely the company will be able to pay off all of its outstanding debt.
Data storage company Storage Dimensions, meanwhile, predicted below expectation second quarter results.
The New York Stock Exchange said that session one had a volume of 1,300, compared with Wednesday's 500. In session two, volume fell to 6.45 million from 10.03 million the previous day.
